root_cause_analysis.symptom: Spec §5.3.D bullet 5 unimplemented: three subagent control cards (spawn/wait/close) render as three scattered cards instead of one merged subagent lifecycle card showing agent nickname/id, started, completed, final summary.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: The CLI mapper emits one envelope per protocol event (spawn begin/end + wait begin/end + close begin/end) and the app routes each envelope to its own card via _all.tsx:57-61. There is no envelope name representing the lifecycle as a single entity, and the renderer has no cross-message grouping signal to merge the 3 cards. Cycles 2-5 stabilized per-card render (cycle-2 fixed visibleCall identifiers; cycle-2 added CODEX_SUBAGENT_CONTROL_TOOLS to suppress generic content) but did NOT introduce the merge layer, by deliberate scope decision (cycle-4 explicitly deferred D.5 to a separate cycle).
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — this is an enhancement (not a regression). Prior cycles' commits stabilized per-card render but explicitly did not address the merge.
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Per the architect memo, the 3-envelope emission was the natural mapping of the Codex collab_agent_call_begin/end protocol events. Cycles 1-2 prioritized DORMANT renderer scaffolding + per-card stability over multi-card merge.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: User spec §5.3.D bullet 4 + bullet 5 explicitly call out that 'three control cards scattered as misleading running command cards' is the wrong UX and 最佳形态 is a single lifecycle card.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Spec §5.3.D first articulated in spec-20260506-203844 cycle 1 (2026-05-04). Bullets 1-4 + 6 closed by cycle 2 (2026-05-04 night). Bullet 5 deferred at cycle-4 (2026-05-07) explicitly. Cycle 6 (this cycle, 2026-05-08) closes bullet 5.

novelty_check.rationale: Prior attempts targeted L1 (registry), L3 (visible-call identifier), L4 (generic-content suppression on already-existing envelopes). No prior attempt synthesized a NEW envelope name nor coordinated cross-envelope suppression keyed by sessionSubagent. The architect memo establishes that L4 (logic at the mapper to emit a 4th envelope) is the only layer where canonical begin/end ordering AND receiverThreadId→sessionSubagent linkage are both available; renderer-only requires non-existent stateful pre-pass infrastructure; mapper-only collapse breaks retroactive compat. Hybrid is the only approach that satisfies both the user need and cycle-2 stability.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: (1) Hybrid is the right approach for D.5 (renderer-only is brittle, mapper-only insufficient); keep it tightly limited to protocol/type, CLI mapper, app normalization/rendering, fixtures/tests. (2) The 4 extractSubtitle vitest tests are likely scope-extending; the user need is '3 control cards into 1 lifecycle card,' not Playwright subtitle hardening — defer them. (3) Translations as observation is defensible if already verified as real native form; do not edit translation files. (4) One cycle is acceptable for D.5 alone; defer the extractSubtitle tests to a future cleanup cycle. (5) Main over-engineering risk is broad renderer abstraction or unrelated UI cleanup — keep the implementation narrow.
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Demoted the 4 extractSubtitle vitest tests from 'secondary in-scope' to W7 (Won't Have) and Out-of-Scope Observations row 3. Translations remain as Out-of-Scope Observations row 4. D.5 hybrid scope tightened to mapper + renderer + suppression + fixtures + tests only; no peripheral cleanup. The spec's Won't Have section explicitly lists W3/W4 (no expand-on-tap UI; no Codex protocol negotiation for agent_nickname) to prevent scope creep into phase-2 work.
